title: Anyone doing everything by hand on side little projects?
author: HereToLearn321
selftext:
Any kinda do this for fun, just "everything" from scratch?

Kinda same ideas as maybe limiting usage of assets, obviously there's a limit since you aren't going to code your own OS or most likely own game engine. But kinda all "game code" , "visuals" and "music" made by you?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I was already doing gamedev as a hobby before AI. as someone who "been there, done that", no thanks

replies.author: RedTheRobot
replies.body: lol. This was my thought. I have done by hand. Now I want be the game designer and have AI build everything, music, art, code, you name it.

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body: I have been programming for 20 years, i was an unsuccessful music producer the past 3 - 5 years, I have had AI build a DAW to generate any kind of music I want for my games, and built a game dev tool with the help of AI to build my games, so I dont have to keep using AI to make my project 🤣

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
you can always join some game jams on itch. there are 3-day ones, 1-week ones, month-long ones etc. 

even before AI, those skills aren't actually valuable because indie game dev is completely different than professional game dev so those skills aren't even transferable. 

and those micro-games/demo basically get 0 attentions outside of jams. 

I mean, it is a grind you can still do if you want but it is just not worthwhile unless you are completely new and you want to build some fundamentals without relying AI 

the worst part about this is that you grind tutorials to finally be able to do something, and then everyone thinks you are bad and those ex-AAA/ex-studio-indie turned solo devs would just clown you because they know how to do things professionally and you don't. 

may as well just use AI honestly.

replies.author: artsmacau
replies.body:
wait what? in which way for example an unreal indie dev skill is not transferable to pro level game dev, if you say amateur devs with no shipped games yes but not transferable? many indie devs have better art skills than game dev graduates, better games too, have you seen the latest indie games outputs? 

i wholy disagree with parts of your comment, people should get the fundamentals then move to AI, otherwise all that is being is using a gigantic amount of tokens to create demo games, and a butload of money to fix what you don't understand, i think its most useful to experienced devs who know what they want to get from their AI agents.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
game dev graduates are still indie/hobbyist. I am referring to people who actually spent time in the industry for some number of years. 

by the way, courses you find online are usually not good enough. those tutors themselves are not that good. yes, you got people from the industry who provide paid courses... but you really can't just grind those tutorial and somehow you are on par with people from the inside

simply using Unreal doesn't mean you are somehow on track to "graduate" into studio-level/AAA-level stuff. it is not how things work...

e.g. you can be using photoshop and some manga studio in japan is also using photoshop. it doesn't mean you have the same photoshop skills or that you will eventually catch up to how they do things with enough photoshop tutorials. 

trust me, indie fundamentals are just for indie stuff. 

also, another big thing is specialization. People who work in the industry have specialized roles. Being a generalist isn't really that helpful to them. 

if you are serious about improving your craft to catch up to the pros, you really should forget about indie gamedev completely, pick a lane (concept art design, level design, special effects, etc) grind that... and then try to get a job in the industry. 

its like anything else tbh. just because you have the same kitchen set used by the pros, you dont just become a pro eventually. Taking random courses wont get you close to that either. People who cook for fun and people cook professionally are on two different paths.

replies.author: artsmacau
replies.body:
makes sense, you made valid points, personally i have no interest in 3A development, im already old and the types of games i want to make are games of my childhood more like a bucket list of games i would love to do, no more complex than a ps2 level game for example, but mostly what games are doing in the indie scene, for an example that hit right away with your example is the clompex nature of mocap and all that goes around it, i bought onimusha and the characters flamboyant comedy style and timing is just something you know an indie dev couldn't make it.

i personally can't consider clair obscur as indie dev, they have extensive experience before.

but again you made excellent points and thank you for taking the time to explain them.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
well, mocap isn't off limit to indie anymore and you dont need an expensive studio setup for it. still, without mocap actors, the quality wont be there obviously... there is student film level mocap, commerical game level mocap, etc

yeah no problem. 

since you decide that you are just cooking for fun then it is all good. I was just cautioning you in case you are some teens/20 something trying to break into the industry. then you def want to pivot away from this...
